In the underground heaven beneath the orchard, past where the rhizome spreads its golden network, exists the Bureau of Ancient Scribbles—a library suspended between centuries where every body is a manuscript and every manuscript breathes.

Eugene, Oregon - 2019

Found them in the compost bin. Not metaphorically. Lisa had thrown the unsigned divorce papers in with the coffee grounds and rotting lettuce. When I asked why, she said, "Everything decomposes eventually."

We'd been attending couples therapy with a woman who called herself a "relationship composter." $200/hour to be told our marriage needed to break down naturally. Lisa took it literally.

My credentials: Twenty years as conservator specializing in palimpsests and destroyed cultural artifacts. Daughter of Syrian manuscript illuminators whose workshop was bombed. Developer of "spectral recovery"—using multispectral imaging to resurrect erased histories.
